sourceEvidence.text: Biscuit ultimately reflects a Latin expression for bread baked twice, transmitted through French and related Romance forms. The historical elements are bis, twice, and a form meaning cooked or baked. This explains the old hard baked food name, not a rule that every food now called a biscuit must be baked twice. American and British food uses later diverged.
